name: Clenbuterol
lead: Clenbuterol is a long-acting beta-2 adrenergic receptor agonist developed as a bronchodilator for asthma and airway obstruction. It is prescribed in some countries for respiratory disease and in veterinary medicine, mainly for horses, but it is not approved for human use in the United States [1][2]. It is on prohibited-substance lists in sport, and a 1995 review described its popularity with athletes for purported anabolic effects and reduction of subcutaneous fat [2][1].

Its use for fat loss and muscle retention is outside any approved indication. Rodent studies from the 1980s reported effects on body composition and muscle growth [16][17], while a 2025 randomized trial in 11 healthy men found increased lean mass and muscle protein accretion alongside reduced cardiorespiratory fitness and desensitization of muscle beta-2 signalling [6]. A systematic review of case reports in athletes described cardiac events including tachycardia, atrial fibrillation, myocarditis, myocardial infarction and death [4].
On looksmax.org, users discuss clenbuterol as a cheap fat-loss pill for getting lean, often compared with GLP-1 drugs and stacked with other compounds [27][28][29][32].

paras: Clenbuterol was introduced as an asthma bronchodilator, with approvals in Germany reported from 1977 and in other countries including Mexico [1]. A 2024 trial compared an ambroxol and clenbuterol oral solution with a Chinese medicine product in children with acute bronchitis [7]. Veterinary papers describe its use to relax the uterus in large-animal obstetrics [8]. Researchers have also tested it in chronic heart failure, where lean mass rose without an endurance improvement, and registered trials in ALS, Pompe disease, spinal and bulbar muscular atrophy and FSHD [10][19][22][23][18].
Athletes and bodybuilders take it for perceived fat reduction and muscle preservation [2][4]. Reviews of weight-loss agents list it among drugs sold online [5]. This article does not provide dosing.

The 2025 Journal of Physiology randomized controlled trial gave healthy men oral clenbuterol or placebo in two 2-week cycles separated by a washout, and reported increased lean mass and muscle protein accretion, reduced cardiorespiratory fitness and blunted muscle beta-2 adrenergic signalling; its authors describe the drug as previously unexplored in randomized trials for these purposes [6]. A heart-failure trial reported more lean muscle mass but no endurance benefit [10], and a combined drug and ventricular assist device protocol that included clenbuterol studied myocardial recovery [12][13][20]. Registered studies include a trial on muscle memory with resistance training, studies of beta-2 stimulation and muscle glucose uptake and a study of responses in healthy humans [21][24][25][26]. A cognition study compared three beta-adrenoceptor drugs in healthy volunteers and Parkinson's disease [9].

A 2023 systematic review of 23 reports covering 24 athletes found supraventricular tachycardia, atrial fibrillation, hypotension, chest pain, myocardial injury, myocarditis, ischemia, infarction, cardiomyopathy, hepatomegaly, hyperglycemia and death, with cardiac complications most common [4]. Individual case reports describe clenbuterol-induced myocarditis [11]. Grokipedia also reports poisoning outbreaks from contaminated veal liver in Spain and France in 1990 [1]. Contaminated or mislabeled supplements have been documented in doping analyses [15].

Clenbuterol selectively stimulates beta-2 adrenoceptors, relaxing bronchial smooth muscle through cyclic AMP, with a longer duration than salbutamol or isoprenaline in guinea pig tissue [1][3][14]. Its effects on muscle and fat are attributed to beta-2 signalling in those tissues [16][6].

Per Grokipedia, Boehringer Ingelheim synthesized the compound in 1967, Germany approved it in 1977, the US approved a veterinary syrup in 1998 and banned it in food animals in 1991, and the EU prohibited beta-agonist growth promotion in 1996 [1]. A 1995 review noted athlete use and a US Olympic Committee ban [2].

Sport anti-doping bodies prohibit it [2][1]. Forum threads on looksmax.org include questions from teenagers about using it to get abs and discussions of ordering it from online pharmacies [27][28]. A 2020 T Nation post describes it as keeping the poster alert on night shifts [33].

lore.intro: On looksmax.org, clenbuterol is treated as an inexpensive oral fat-loss drug, often named alongside cardarine, DNP, HGH and GLP-1 compounds [27][28][29][32].

claims.claim: Clen is a cheap way to get shredded
claims.believers: A user reports seeing good progress in others and notes the low price per tablet and a dislike of GLP-1 agonists [28]. Another thread asks about starting it for abs after a year of lifting [27].
claims.experts: A randomized trial in healthy men found increased lean mass but reduced fitness, and the athlete case literature documents cardiac harms; no trial tests it for fat loss in healthy people [6][4].

claims.claim: Clen is stronger than GW (cardarine) but has worse side effects
claims.believers: A poster in a clen versus cardarine thread says clen sides are worse but that clen is stronger [29].
claims.experts: No published comparison exists; reports describe cardiac adverse events with clenbuterol [4].

claims.believers: A looksmax.org thread asks whether clenbuterol causes more vascularity [31].
claims.experts: No published studies were found on vascularity; documented effects include tachycardia and hypotension [4].

claims.claim: Clen plus DNP and other drugs produce dramatic transformations
claims.believers: Users discuss running clen with HGH, cardarine and DNP and debate transformation results [30][32].
claims.experts: A review of weight-loss toxicity covers DNP and other agents sold online, and case reports document serious adverse events with clenbuterol [5][4].

card.summary: Asthma-drug stimulant used as a gray-market cutting pill, with a documented record of heart problems.
card.note: Not approved for humans in the US; case reports of arrhythmia, myocarditis and death; banned in sport.

quick.overview:
Clenbuterol is a beta-2 agonist made as an asthma bronchodilator. It is not approved for people in the US but is bought online by bodybuilders and others for fat loss.

The only randomized trial in healthy men reported added lean mass but poorer cardiorespiratory fitness.
quick.mechanism: It activates beta-2 adrenergic receptors, which relax airways and, in muscle and fat tissue, are linked to protein accretion and fat breakdown. Receptors can become less responsive with repeated use.
quick.risks: Case reports in athletes describe fast heartbeat, atrial fibrillation, chest pain, myocarditis, heart attack and death. It is banned in sport and in food animals, and unregulated supply can be mislabeled or contaminated.
